channel.title: Nature Chemistry
channel.description: Nature Chemistry is a monthly journal dedicated to publishing high-quality papers that describe the most significant and cutting-edge research in all areas of chemistry. As well as reflecting the traditional core subjects of analytical, inorganic, organic and physical chemistry, the journal features a broad range of chemical research including, but not limited to, bioinorganic and bioorganic chemistry, catalysis, computational and theoretical chemistry, environmental chemistry, green chemistry, medicinal chemistry, organometallic chemistry, polymer chemistry, supramolecular chemistry and surface chemistry. Other multidisciplinary topics such as nanotechnology, chemical biology and materials chemistry are also featured.

item.title: Coherent manipulation of Zr(III) aryloxide qudits
item.content:encoded:
Nature Chemistry, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41557-026-02269-5

Zr(III) complexes have been historically challenging to isolate owing to their tendency to dimerize or disproportionate. Now, bulky aryloxide ligands have been used to kinetically stabilize mononuclear Zr(III) ions at room temperature. The electronic and electronuclear transitions of these complexes can also be coherently manipulated as competitive molecular qudits.

item.title: Cooling water to near freezing breaks the activity–stability trade-off of water oxidation electrocatalysis
item.content:encoded:
Nature Chemistry, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41557-026-02274-8

Temperature can influence competing catalytic pathways differently, but its role in balancing electrocatalytic activity and stability remains underexplored. Now it has been shown that cooling water to near freezing selectively suppresses manganese dioxide dissolution, extending water oxidation lifetime and revealing anomalous subzero kinetics.
item.dc:title: Cooling water to near freezing breaks the activity–stability trade-off of water oxidation electrocatalysis

item.title: Electrolytes that mind bridging the gap
item.content:encoded:
Nature Chemistry, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41557-026-02287-3

Silicon anodes enable high-energy-density Li-ion batteries but face reversibility challenges when operating under extreme temperature and charge-rate conditions. Now, a liquid electrolyte design results in interface protection and reduced electrode expansion during such operation, while also having lithium plating tolerance.
item.dc:title: Electrolytes that mind bridging the gap
item.dc:creator: Fokko M. Mulder

item.title: Stereochemical preorganization directs triple-helical assembly of Au<sub>4</sub> nanoclusters
item.content:encoded:
Nature Chemistry, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41557-026-02271-x

Translating local stereochemical information into higher-order helical architectures is a central challenge in materials design. Now it has been shown that stereochemically preorganized Au4 nanoclusters assemble into homochiral triple helices through directional aurophilic interactions, providing a design strategy for chiral nanocluster materials with amplified chiroptical responses.
item.dc:title: Stereochemical preorganization directs triple-helical assembly of Au<sub>4</sub> nanoclusters
